title: Bindaetteok (Korean mung bean pancake)

ingredients.name: dried peeled mung beans, soaked 4 hours

steps: Drain the beans and blend them with 150 ml of water and the salt into a coarse, thick batter.
Mix in the kimchi, pork, bean sprouts, spring onions and garlic.
Heat generous oil in a frying pan over medium heat.
Spoon the batter in to form pancakes about 10 cm wide and 1 cm thick.
Fry for 4 to 5 minutes per side until deep golden and crisp at the edges.
Serve hot with a dipping sauce of soy sauce and vinegar.

title: Dak galbi (Korean spicy stir-fried chicken)

ingredients.name: boneless chicken thighs, cut into bite-size pieces

steps: Mix the gochujang, chili flakes, soy sauce, sugar and garlic and coat the chicken in it. Marinate at least 30 minutes.
Heat the oil in a wide, heavy pan and add the sweet potato and a splash of water, covering for 3 minutes to soften it.
Add the chicken and cook over medium-high heat for about 8 minutes, stirring.
Add the cabbage and onion and cook, stirring, until the chicken is cooked through and the vegetables have wilted, about 8 minutes more.
Stir in the perilla leaves at the end and serve from the pan with rice or lettuce leaves.

title: Doenjang jjigae (Korean fermented soybean paste stew)
steps: Bring the stock to a boil in a pot and dissolve the soybean paste in it, using a sieve or spoon so no lumps remain.
Add the potato and onion and simmer for 8 minutes.
Add the zucchini, garlic and chili flakes and cook for 5 more minutes.
Add the tofu and sliced chili and simmer gently for 3 minutes.
Taste, thinning with a splash of water if too salty, scatter over the spring onion and serve with rice.

title: Galbitang (Korean short rib soup)

ingredients.name: beef short ribs, cut into pieces
egg, scrambled into thin sheets and sliced

steps: Soak the ribs in cold water for 30 minutes, then blanch them in boiling water for 5 minutes and rinse to remove scum.
Return the ribs to a clean pot with the water and garlic and simmer gently for 1 hour.
Add the radish and soy sauce and simmer 40 minutes more until the meat is tender.
Add the noodles in the last 5 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper and serve topped with spring onions and egg strips.

title: Gamjatang (Korean pork bone and potato stew)
steps: Soak the bones in cold water for an hour to draw out the blood, then boil for 10 minutes and rinse well.
Return the bones to a clean pot with the water and simmer for 40 minutes.
Mix the chili flakes, doenjang, soy sauce, garlic and ginger into a paste.
Stir the paste into the pot, add the potatoes and cook for 25 minutes until the potatoes are soft.
Add the cabbage or perilla leaves and spring onions and cook 5 minutes more.
Serve with rice.

title: Gyeran jjim (Korean steamed egg)
steps: Beat the eggs well, then stir in the stock and salt, and strain through a sieve for a smooth custard.
Pour into a small heavy pot or a ttukbaegi and place over medium-low heat.
Stir constantly with a spoon for a couple of minutes until the egg begins to set into curds.
Cover with a lid, reduce to the lowest heat and cook for 8 to 10 minutes until puffed and just set.
Finish with spring onion, a drop of sesame oil and sesame seeds. Serve in the pot.

title: Hotteok (Korean sweet filled pancake)
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and salt with the warm milk to form a sticky dough, cover and let it rise for 1 hour until doubled.
Mix the brown sugar, cinnamon and nuts for the filling.
With oiled hands, divide the dough into 8 pieces and flatten each into a disc.
Put a spoonful of filling into the middle and pinch closed, then flatten gently.
Cook in an oiled pan over medium-low heat for 3 minutes, press flat with a spatula and flip, cooking another 3 minutes until golden and the sugar has melted into a syrup.
Cool slightly before biting, since the filling is very hot.

title: Jajangmyeon (Korean noodles in black bean sauce)

ingredients.name: chunjang (Korean black bean paste; or Chinese sweet bean sauce)
potato starch mixed with 3 tbsp water

steps: Fry the black bean paste in 2 tablespoons of oil over low heat for about 3 minutes to cook out its bitterness, then remove it from the pan.
Heat the remaining oil and brown the pork, then add the onion, potato and zucchini and stir-fry for 5 minutes.
Return the paste to the pan, add the sugar and 350 ml of water and simmer for 10 minutes until the vegetables are soft.
Stir in the starch slurry and cook for a minute until the sauce thickens and turns glossy.
Cook the noodles in boiling water until tender, drain and divide into bowls.
Spoon the sauce over the noodles and top with cucumber matchsticks. Toss everything together at the table.

title: Japchae (Korean glass noodles with vegetables and beef)

ingredients.name: dried shiitake mushrooms, soaked and sliced

steps: Boil the noodles for about 6 minutes until soft and slippery, rinse under cold water, drain well and cut them a few times with scissors so they are easier to eat.
Blanch the spinach for 30 seconds, squeeze out the water and season it with a little soy sauce, sesame oil and garlic.
Marinate the beef and mushrooms with a tablespoon of soy sauce, a teaspoon of sugar, garlic and a drizzle of sesame oil for 10 minutes.
Stir-fry the onion and carrot separately in a little oil, each just until tender but still bright, and set them aside.
Cook the beef and mushrooms in the same pan until browned.
In a large pan or bowl, toss the noodles with the remaining soy sauce, sugar and sesame oil over low heat until they take on a glossy brown colour.
Mix in all the vegetables and meat, sprinkle with sesame seeds and serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Kalguksu (Korean knife-cut noodle soup)

ingredients.name: fresh kalguksu or flat wheat noodles

steps: Bring the stock to a simmer with the potato and cook for 5 minutes.
Shake the loose flour off the noodles and add them to the pot, stirring so they don't clump.
Add the zucchini and clams or chicken, soy sauce and garlic and cook for 5 to 6 minutes until the noodles are tender.
The flour on the noodles will thicken the broth lightly.
Pour in the beaten egg in a thin stream, scatter over the spring onions and serve very hot.

title: Kimchi jjigae (Korean kimchi and pork stew)
steps: Heat the sesame oil in a heavy pot and fry the pork until the edges turn golden.
Add the kimchi, onion and garlic and stir-fry for 4 to 5 minutes until the kimchi softens and smells sweetly sour.
Stir in the chili flakes and sugar, then pour in the water or stock.
Bring to a boil, reduce the heat and simmer for 20 minutes so the flavours deepen.
Lay in the tofu and simmer for another 5 minutes.
Scatter over the spring onions and serve bubbling hot with steamed rice.

title: Kongnamul muchim (Korean seasoned soybean sprouts)
steps: Rinse the soybean sprouts and pick over them, discarding any rotten ones.
Boil them in a covered pot with a little water for 6 to 7 minutes, keeping the lid on so they don't taste raw.
Drain and cool in a bowl.
Toss with the garlic, salt, sesame oil, spring onion and chili flakes if wanted.
Finish with sesame seeds and serve at room temperature or chilled.

title: Mandu (Korean pork and kimchi dumplings)

ingredients.name: kimchi, finely chopped and squeezed dry
mung bean sprouts, blanched and chopped

steps: Mix the pork, kimchi, tofu, bean sprouts, garlic, soy sauce and sesame oil thoroughly into a firm filling.
Place a spoonful in the centre of a wrapper, moisten the edge with water, fold in half and pinch tightly closed.
Boil, steam or pan-fry. To pan-fry, heat the oil in a non-stick pan and place the dumplings flat side down.
Fry until golden underneath, then add a splash of water and cover to steam for 5 minutes.
Serve with a dipping sauce of soy sauce and vinegar.

title: Miyeok-guk (Korean seaweed soup)

ingredients.name: beef brisket or shoulder, thinly sliced

steps: Soak the seaweed in cold water for 20 to 30 minutes until fully expanded, then rinse and cut into short lengths.
Heat the sesame oil in a pot and stir-fry the beef with half the garlic until it changes colour.
Add the seaweed and the soy sauce and stir for 2 to 3 minutes.
Pour in the water and bring to a boil.
Lower the heat and simmer for 30 to 40 minutes until the broth turns milky and the seaweed is silky.
Season with salt and the remaining garlic and serve with rice.

title: Naengmyeon (Korean cold buckwheat noodles)

ingredients.name: small Korean pear or cucumber, thinly sliced
cooked beef slices (from making the broth)

steps: Season the cold broth with vinegar, sugar, mustard and salt, and keep it in the freezer until slushy at the edges.
Boil the noodles for 1 to 2 minutes only, as thin buckwheat noodles cook fast.
Rinse the noodles under cold water, rubbing them gently to remove the starch, and drain thoroughly.
Divide the noodles into bowls and arrange the beef, pear, cucumber and egg on top.
Pour in the icy broth and add extra vinegar and mustard at the table to taste.

title: Pajeon (Korean spring onion pancake)
steps: Whisk both flours with the salt, cold water and egg into a thin batter, like thin cream.
Stir the soy sauce, vinegar and chili flakes together for the dipping sauce.
Heat a tablespoon of oil in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat.
Lay the spring onions in the pan in parallel rows, pour batter over them to bind them, and cook for 3 to 4 minutes until golden underneath.
Add a little more oil around the edge, flip and press lightly, then cook until crisp, about 3 minutes.
Cut into squares and serve hot with the sauce.

title: Samgyeopsal (Korean grilled pork belly)

ingredients.name: pork belly, sliced about 1 cm thick

steps: Pat the pork dry and season with salt and pepper.
Combine the sesame oil with a pinch of salt for dipping.
Heat a heavy griddle or cast-iron pan until very hot.
Cook the pork slices in a single layer for 3 to 4 minutes per side until deeply browned and crisp, grilling the garlic alongside.
Cut the pork into bite-size pieces with scissors.
Wrap a piece in a lettuce leaf with garlic, a dab of ssamjang and a slice of chili, and eat in one bite.

title: Samgyetang (Korean ginseng chicken soup)

ingredients.name: small whole young chickens (about 600 g each) or poussins

steps: Drain the rice and divide it between the two birds along with 3 garlic cloves, 2 jujubes and a ginseng root each, filling loosely because rice swells.
Cross the legs and tuck them in or tie them so the stuffing stays put.
Place the birds in a deep pot, add the remaining garlic and the water and bring to a boil.
Reduce to a gentle simmer, cover and cook for 50 to 60 minutes until the chicken is falling-tender and the rice cooked.
Season the broth with salt to taste and serve each bird in its own bowl with spring onions and pepper.

title: Sundubu jjigae (Korean soft tofu stew)
steps: Heat the sesame oil in a small heavy pot, add the pork and cook for a couple of minutes.
Stir in the garlic and chili flakes for 30 seconds, taking care not to scorch them.
Add the stock and soy sauce and bring to a boil.
Add the clams or shrimp and simmer until the clams open.
Spoon in the tofu in large pieces without stirring too much, and simmer for 4 minutes.
Crack in the egg, scatter over the spring onions and bring the pot straight to the table, still bubbling.

title: Tteokbokki (Korean spicy stir-fried rice cakes)
steps: Soak the rice cakes in cold water for 20 minutes if they are hard or refrigerated.
Whisk the gochujang, chili flakes, soy sauce and sugar into the stock in a wide pan and bring to a boil.
Add the rice cakes and fish cake and simmer, stirring often so they do not stick, for 10 to 12 minutes.
When the sauce is thick and clings to the rice cakes, add the spring onions and halved eggs.
Cook for 2 more minutes and serve immediately while the rice cakes are chewy.

title: Tteokguk (Korean rice cake soup for the New Year)
steps: Simmer the beef in the water for 40 minutes, skimming the foam, then lift it out and shred it.
Soak the rice cakes in cold water for 20 minutes and drain.
Season the broth with soy sauce, garlic and salt if needed.
Add the rice cakes and cook for 5 to 7 minutes until soft and floating.
Beat the eggs, pour them in a thin stream and let them set in strands.
Ladle into bowls and top with beef, spring onions, seaweed and sesame oil.

title: Yukgaejang (Korean spicy beef and scallion soup)

ingredients.name: spring onions, cut into long lengths

steps: Simmer the beef in the water for about an hour until tender, then remove and shred along the grain.
Mix the shredded beef with chili flakes, soy sauce, garlic and sesame oil to make a red paste.
Fry the paste briefly in a pot, then pour the beef broth over it.
Add the bean sprouts and spring onions and simmer 15 minutes.
Add the soaked vermicelli if using, and drizzle in the beaten eggs.
Season to taste and serve with rice.
